mhF3BkzlTaGiLzJ7kvpmVc:9774-82207.notes: SUBSET MEASURED COMPLETELY AND FIXED: the ticket's 0/25/50/75/100 percent slider, from a census of ALL 122 slider cards and 602 stop labels on page 3:3 rather than from the two or three nodes a single frame offers. TWO DELTAS FIXED. (1) The stops: every 351-wide card (375) and every 698-wide one (768) sets them in Mulish Regular 12/14 -4PERCENT, every 281-wide one (the 313 desktop column) in 11/14, and the component shipped 11/14 at every width - the oracle had PINNED that as a known departure on 2026-09-01 with the numbers written down, and this builds it as text-xs leading-[14px] lg:text-[11px]. ORACLE TicketPercentSlider.figma.test.tsx, now 18 tests, with the label row and the card height derived per board as max(line box, the 44px square index.css puts under a button without the opt-out) - the floor's width and its opt-out read OUT of the stylesheet, not restated. MEASURED, NOT FIXED: with a stop selected every frame draws that stop solid and the other four at effective opacity 0.44, which the component already does - but at REST, nothing entered, all five are solid (9058:223785, 9058:223908, 3899:7182..7186) and the component treats 0 as a selection and dims four. 10335-236021.title: Create post - two images
10335-236021.notes: MEASURED IN FULL AND NOT BUILT, BECAUSE BUILDING IT CHANGES A CONTRACT OTHER LANES READ. FIGMA `Frame 1265` is a HORIZONTAL auto-layout, gap 8, holding two tiles that each FILL half of it: at 1440 (`10335:236102`) 460 wide over two 226 x 198.798 tiles at cornerRadius 12, each with a 36 x 36 circular remove control filled #001615 at opacity 0.44 inset 16 from the top and right (`10335:236037`, `10335:236093`); at 375 (`11527:291915`) 330 wide over two 161 x 161 tiles at the same radius with 32 x 32 controls inset 8 (`11527:291917`, `11527:291919`). The column above them, `Frame 1262`, carries itemSpacing 24 at both. CODE the composer holds ONE `imageUrl` in state, renders one full-width preview, and submits `{content, imageUrl, cashtag}`; `socialFeedService.createPost` takes a single `image_url` (`:232`, `:256`, `:430`). So a second image has nowhere to go without widening `FeedPost.media`, `feedSource`'s mapping and `PostCard`'s reader, all of which other lanes read. TWO OPTIONS: (a) ship two-image posts end to end - carry the second URL in the `posts.metadata` jsonb the service already writes (`socialFeedService.ts:443`), widen `FeedPost.media` to a list, and render `Frame 1265` in both the composer and the card, which needs no schema change; or (b) rule the state out of the product and record `10335:236021` / `11527:291862` as a drawing we do not offer, so the pair stops reading as unbuilt work. NOT GUESSED EITHER WAY - a composer that accepts two files and posts one is the shape of defect this repo has been burned by.

11474-222012.title: Skai > Social > Sample creator profile > Posts (1440 x 900px)
11474-222012.notes: STILL BLOCKED, BUT THE RECORDED CAUSE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECT ONE IS A DIFFERENT PIECE OF WORK. The reason this row carried - there is no post entity - is true of Postgres and FALSE of the system: the contract declares createPost(bytes32 contentHash, uint256 parentId), the chain package types a SocialPost with id, author, contentHash, parentId, blockNum and txHash, and the indexer routes GET on the social feed. PROBED LIVE THIS SESSION against the public RPC. The social-feed predeploy holds exactly 55 bytes and they are the standard proxy runtime; its implementation slot points at a second address whose code is the SAME 55 bytes, so the delegatecall lands on a proxy pointing at itself and every read reverts with a stack underflow of 5 against 6. A control call on the same endpoint answers correctly - the stable token reports 6 decimals - so this is the contract, not the node. So the schedule item is A REDEPLOY, not a schema design, and those are not the same work. NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: contentHash is a bytes32, so the post BODY is not on chain and has no off-chain store, and the feed payload carries no author handle and no like count. Even with posts flowing, every card in this masonry would draw caption-less and author-less. The tab renders an explicit unavailable state, which is the right outcome under either cause. Frame defect unchanged: harvested 375x1365 while the registry files it at viewport 1440x900.

Nightmare (4 tiles, 1 safe) goes from 0.95x4^6 = 3891.2x to 0.95x4^9 = 249036.8x, i.e. 64 TIMES today's ceiling on the tier the cap exists for; extreme goes 6232.95x to 18698.85x; and the three safe tiers are CUT at the top -- easy 16.87x to 12.65x, medium 54.7817x to 36.5212x, hard 972.8x to 486.4x. Re-read 2026-09-01: supabase/functions/_shared/videoPoker.ts VP_PAYTABLE (:36-46) ships Royal Flush 800, Straight Flush 50, Four of a Kind 25, Full House 9, Flush 6, Straight 4, Three of a Kind 3, Two Pair 2, Jacks or Better 1. So 800x MATCHES the rail exactly and only TWO of the nine rows diverge: Straight Flush 60 vs 50 and Four of a Kind 22 vs 25. The 800x royal is the max-coin schedule that gives 9/6 Jacks or Better its 99.54% RTP; a 250x royal would cap it near 98.2%. The frame-defect verdict is unchanged -- what is corrected is the reason, which filed a matching value as evidence of the defect on eight rows running. GUARDED IN CODE: videoPokerPaytable.test.tsx asserts every rendered multiplier equals the server table parsed off disk AND that the literals 60 and 22 never reach the module.
